content.text: {"statements":{"L6.1":{"established":"partial","quote":"**Theorem A (proved):** for all $n$, $a_{n+1}$ = successor of $a_n$ in $S_\\infty=\\bigcap_m S_m$; hence the sequence is EXACTLY $S_\\infty\\cap[a_1,\\infty)$.","note":"The characterization is stated, but no proof is included."},"L6.2":{"established":"no","quote":null,"note":"Finiteness is explicitly identified as the remaining unproved crux; numerical evidence does not establish it."},"L6.3":{"established":"partial","quote":"So it suffices: $S_\\infty$ is a union of residue classes mod $L$ (then $a_{n+T}=a_n+L$ for ALL $n$ with $T=\\#(S_\\infty\\cap[1,L])$).","note":"The periodicity assembly is only conditional; finite-prime dependence and an actual valid L are not proved."}},"S_ref":0,"notes":"The write-up gives a useful conditional framework, but supplies no written proof of characterization and expressly leaves the essential finiteness lemma open. Consequently global periodicity is not established."}
